title: Subtoken causality traces for KV cache and batching latency attribution
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: instrument causal links between individual subtokens (wordpiece/bytepair units) and downstream sources of latency and cost: specifically KV cache hits/misses and batch scheduling delays. We need spans/markers that let us answer questions like: for request X, which subtokens incurred additional 95th/99th latency due to cache misses or being pushed into a later batch? This ticket designs and implements end-to-end traces plus aggregation pipelines to produce per-token attribution metrics and dashboard surfaces.

Scope and deliverables:
- Define a compact span model for subtokens that is safe to emit at production scale (attributes, sampling, deterministic IDs).
- Implement tracing hooks inside the serving runtime to attach subtoken spans at: tokenizer output, pre-batch queue, kernel dispatch, KV cache lookup, and emission commit.
- Add deterministic causality IDs so a subtoken span can be correlated across processes/nodes when requests are sharded.
- Ship micro-sampler with adjustable rate + reservoir logic (prefer burst-aware targeting for tail latencies).
- Extend metrics/log aggregation pipeline (OTLP -> kafka -> stream processor) to derive: per-subtoken latency delta attributable to KV cache miss, batch delay, and kernel queuing.
- Dashboard and alerting: new token-attribution dashboard (per-model, per-route) and SLO bleed-down alerts when per-token cost grows beyond baseline.

Design decisions / trade-offs considered:
- Full-fidelity per-subtoken spans would be prohibitive for high-qps customers; settled on a hybrid: deterministic hash-based target sampling (1:100 default) + dynamic upsampling for requests that hit tail latency thresholds. This balances visibility with telemetry bill.
- Span shape: keep span payload minimal (subtoken_id, relative_offset_in_req, event_type, causality_id, cache_hit:boolean, kernel_stage:string, ns_latency:int). Avoid embedding full prompt text in spans to reduce PII risk.
- Causality ID generation: use 128-bit UUID derived from request_id + subtoken index to allow cross-node joins without global coordination.
- Storage/rollups: compute per-request aggregates in stream processing (kafka->flink), emit summarized per-route/per-model metrics to long-term TSDB. Retain raw sampled traces in trace-store for 7 days.

Migration/rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): enable hooks in runtime with sampling disabled; validate span schema end-to-end using internal load tests (perf/regression).
- Phase 2 (low-volume customers): enable sampling=1% for internal and selected beta customers; monitor telemetry volume and latency overhead.
- Phase 3 (gradual ramp): enable dynamic upsampling targeting requests with >95th latency; build dashboards and iterate.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end trace chain for sampled requests shows subtokens through pre-batch -> kv lookup -> kernel dispatch -> emission commit across nodes.
- Stream processor outputs per-subtoken delta metrics with <2% false attribution in synthetic bench.
- Runtime CPU overhead <= 1.5% p95 at sampling=1%, and memory overhead <10MB per worker for tracing buffers.

Notes and links to artifacts: see design doc and proto for span schema, sampling strategy, and aggregation queries.
